questions.question: Which of the following reactions will yield 1-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane as the major product?
options: 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HBr in the presence of peroxide
3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HBr in the absence of peroxide
2,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HBr in the presence of peroxide
3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HCl in the presence of peroxide
questions.solution:
The target product is 1-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane, which is a primary alkyl bromide.

To obtain a primary alkyl bromide from a terminal alkene without altering the carbon skeleton, anti-Markovnikov addition is required. This is achieved by the reaction of the alkene with HBr in the presence of a peroxide (Kharasch effect).

The starting alkene must have the same carbon skeleton. Thus, 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene reacting with HBr and peroxide will yield 1-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane.

In the absence of peroxide, HBr would undergo Markovnikov addition with a methyl shift, yielding 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane. HCl does not exhibit the peroxide effect and would follow Markovnikov's rule.

Answer: 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HBr in the presence of peroxide

questions.question: An alkene with the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ yields only a single type of carbonyl compound upon reductive ozonolysis. If the alkene also exhibits geometrical isomerism, its IUPAC name is
questions.solution:
The alkene yields only a single type of carbonyl compound upon reductive ozonolysis, which indicates that it must be a symmetrical alkene. For the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$, the possible symmetrical acyclic alkenes are hex-3-ene and 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene. Cyclohexene is a cyclic alkene that also yields a single product (hexanedial) upon ozonolysis.

The question states that the alkene exhibits geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism. For geometrical isomerism to occur, each carbon atom of the double bond must be attached to two different groups.

In 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, each double-bonded carbon is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.
Cyclohexene does not exhibit geometrical isomerism because the trans-isomer is highly strained and does not exist under normal conditions.
Hex-2-ene shows geometrical isomerism but yields two different products (ethanal and butanal) on ozonolysis.
Hex-3-ene ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) is symmetrical (yielding only propanal on ozonolysis) and each double-bonded carbon is attached to a hydrogen atom and an ethyl group, allowing it to exhibit geometrical isomerism.

Therefore, the alkene is hex-3-ene.

Answer: Hex-3-ene

questions.solution:
Step 1 is the Etard reaction. Toluene is oxidised by chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in $\text{CS}_2$ followed by acid hydrolysis to give benzaldehyde (Compound A).

Step 2 is the nitration of benzaldehyde. The aldehydic group ($-\text{CHO}$) is an electron-withdrawing group and acts as a meta-directing, deactivating group in electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Therefore, nitration of benzaldehyde with a nitrating mixture (concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) yields $m$-nitrobenzaldehyde as the major product (Compound B).

Students who assume the $-\text{CHO}$ group is ortho/para directing will incorrectly choose $o$- or $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde. Students who ignore the reaction sequence and nitrate toluene directly will incorrectly choose $p$-nitrotoluene.

questions.question:
What is the major product formed when $p$-toluidine undergoes the following sequence of reactions?

(i) $\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$, pyridine
(ii) $\text{Br}_2$, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$
(iii) $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$
(iv) $\text{NaNO}_2$, $\text{HCl}$, $273\text{ K}$
(v) $\text{CuCN}$
questions.solution:
The starting material, $p$-toluidine (4-methylaniline), is first treated with acetic anhydride ($\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$) in pyridine to protect the highly reactive $-\text{NH}_2$ group, forming $N$-acetyl-$p$-toluidine.

During bromination ($\text{Br}_2\text{/CH}_3\text{COOH}$), the $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group is a stronger activating and directing group than the $-\text{CH}_3$ group. Thus, the incoming electrophile ($\text{Br}^+$) is directed to the position ortho to the $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group, yielding 2-bromo-4-methylacetanilide.

Acid hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) removes the acetyl protecting group to give 2-bromo-4-methylaniline.

Treatment with $\text{NaNO}_2\text{/HCl}$ at 273 K converts the primary amine into a diazonium salt.

Finally, reaction with $\text{CuCN}$ (Sandmeyer reaction) replaces the diazonium group with a nitrile ($-\text{CN}$) group, resulting in 2-bromo-4-methylbenzonitrile.

Answer: 2-Bromo-4-methylbenzonitrile

questions.solution:
In 2-nitroanisole, the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is strongly activating and ortho/para directing, while the $-\text{NO}_2$ group is deactivating and meta directing. Both groups synergistically direct the incoming electrophile ($\text{Br}^+$) to the position para to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group (position 4) as it is less sterically hindered than the ortho position. This yields 4-bromo-2-nitroanisole.

Treatment with $\text{Sn/HCl}$ reduces the $-\text{NO}_2$ group to an $-\text{NH}_2$ group, forming 4-bromo-2-methoxyaniline.

Reaction with $\text{NaNO}_2\text{/HCl}$ at 273 K converts the amine into a diazonium salt.

Finally, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2\text{/H}_2\text{O}$ reduces the diazonium group to a hydrogen atom (deamination), yielding 4-bromoanisole as the final major product $X$.

Answer: 4-Bromoanisole

When compound $\text{X}$ is heated with concentrated sodium hydroxide, it yields two compounds, $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$. The compounds $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$ are respectively:
questions.question: Benzene reacts with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminum chloride and cuprous chloride to form compound $\text{X}$. When compound $\text{X}$ is heated with concentrated sodium hydroxide, it yields two compounds, $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$. The compounds $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzene with carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) and hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{CuCl}$ is the Gattermann-Koch reaction. The product $\text{X}$ formed is benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$).

Benzaldehyde does not contain any $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms. When heated with a concentrated alkali like concentrated $\text{NaOH}$, aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens undergo the Cannizzaro reaction. This is a disproportionation reaction where one molecule of the aldehyde is reduced to the corresponding alcohol and another is oxidized to the salt of the corresponding carboxylic acid.

Therefore, benzaldehyde disproportionates to yield benzyl alcohol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) and sodium benzoate ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}$).

Thus, compounds $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$ are sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol.

Option (1) is incorrect because it assumes $\text{X}$ is phenol. Option (2) is incorrect because it assumes a simple acid-base neutralization or complete oxidation. Option (4) is incorrect because sodium formate would be a product of a cross-Cannizzaro reaction with formaldehyde.

Answer: Sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol

For example, ozonolysis of 1-methylcyclohexene (which has only one alkyl substituent on the double bond) yields 7-oxoheptanal, which is a keto-aldehyde, not a diketone.

Therefore, Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

The peroxide effect (anti-Markovnikov addition) is observed only with HBr. It is not observed with HCl or HI because one of the steps in their free radical mechanism is endothermic.

Therefore, even in the presence of benzoyl peroxide, the addition of HCl to pent-1-ene follows Markovnikov's rule via an electrophilic addition mechanism.

The proton ($\text{H}^{+}$) adds to the terminal carbon to form the more stable secondary carbocation. The chloride ion ($\text{Cl}^{-}$) then attacks this carbocation to form 2-chloropentane as the major product.

Answer: 2-Chloropentane

questions.solution:
Compound 'A' ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{NO}_2$) is a nitrotoluene.

Reduction of nitrotoluene with $\text{Sn/HCl}$ yields a toluidine ('B').

Diazotization of toluidine followed by hydrolysis (warming with water) yields a cresol ('C').

For a cresol to form a tribromo derivative upon reaction with bromine water, all three positions ortho and para to the activating $-\text{OH}$ group must be unsubstituted.

In $m$-cresol (3-methylphenol), the $-\text{CH}_3$ group is at the meta position, leaving both ortho positions and the para position free for electrophilic aromatic substitution. Thus, it forms 2,4,6-tribromo-3-methylphenol.

In contrast, $o$-cresol and $p$-cresol have one of these positions blocked by the methyl group and can only form dibromo derivatives.

Therefore, 'C' is $m$-cresol, 'B' is $m$-toluidine, and 'A' is $m$-nitrotoluene.

Answer: $m$-Nitrotoluene

questions.question: An alkane with the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}$ undergoes oxidation when treated with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ to yield an alcohol. What is the IUPAC name of the alcohol formed?
questions.solution:
The given molecular formula is $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}$, which corresponds to an alkane. The possible structural isomers for $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}$ are:

2) 2-Methylbutane ($\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$)

Alkanes generally resist oxidation. However, an alkane having a tertiary hydrogen atom can be selectively oxidized to the corresponding alcohol by strong oxidizing agents like $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

Among the isomers of $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}$, only 2-Methylbutane possesses a tertiary hydrogen atom (at C-2). Therefore, it is the isomer that will undergo oxidation.

The oxidation reaction replaces the tertiary hydrogen with a hydroxyl ($-\mathrm{OH}$) group:

The resulting product is 2-Methylbutan-2-ol.

The products of reductive ozonolysis are propanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) and ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$).

Numbering the longest carbon chain to give the double bond the lowest possible number, we get 2-methylbut-2-ene.

2-Methylbut-1-ene yields butan-2-one and methanal.
3-Methylbut-1-ene yields 2-methylpropanal and methanal.
Pent-2-ene yields ethanal and propanal.

Assertion (A) is false. 2,2-Dimethylpropane (neopentane) has the structure $\mathrm{C(CH_3)_4}$. The central carbon is quaternary ($4^{\circ}$) and is bonded to four methyl groups. It does not possess any tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) hydrogen atom. Therefore, it resists oxidation by alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

Reason (R) is true. As a general rule, alkanes are inert towards oxidizing agents. However, as an exception, alkanes containing a tertiary hydrogen atom can be oxidized to the corresponding tertiary alcohol by potassium permanganate ($\mathrm{KMnO}_4$).

Thus, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
